neighbours.label: Purpose/benefit/necessity predicate words (necessary, unnecessary, designed, help, beneficial, 'for') in health and biomedical prose, where a purpose or benefit complement is about to follow
fire: Doctors now agree that surgery is not necessary for most children with mild ear infections.
The new inhaler was designed to deliver the drug straight to the lungs of asthma patients.
Regular walking after a heart attack can help lower blood pressure over several months.
In a patient with diabetes, a small amount of red wine might be beneficial to circulation, according to one small trial.
Her mother had suffered from migraines for most of her adult life, and nobody ever found a cure.
The hospital insisted that the extra scan was totally unnecessary, given how mild the symptoms were.
Researchers say the protein is vital to understanding why some tumours spread while others stay put.
A balanced diet will often help prevent kidney stones in people who are prone to them.
quiet: Doctors now report that most children with mild ear infections recover within a week.
The new inhaler was approved by regulators after trials involving hundreds of asthma patients.
Regular walking after a heart attack was recorded in the clinic's discharge notes of every patient.
At the dinner in the diabetes study, a small amount of red wine was served, according to one small trial.
Her mother had suffered migraines in her twenties, and nobody ever found the cause.
The hospital insisted that the extra scan was scheduled on Tuesday, given how mild the symptoms were.
Researchers say the protein appears in many tissues, including tumours that spread and those that stay put.
The farmer dug a new irrigation channel across the lower field, which stays dry in summer.

notes: 10x pilot (concept-maps/tenx, census arm): label and 16 sentences written by a fresh Sonnet 5.5 subagent from a packet (card + all-pole band samples + concept-census evidence (which concepts and domains selected the pole)); no probes. An Opus gate checked rule-level items only (8 + 8, 0 overlap with census and probe text, near misses free of the declared trigger) and edited nothing. Labeller's note: Strong activations are a diffuse mix: purpose/necessity/benefit words and ' for' mostly in health or biomedical prose; the census shows the pole responding to disease topics in neutral frames. Coverage is likely partial and the label may be too broad.
